points.description: States that a missing base case (no terminating condition / stopping condition) causes infinite recursion. Equivalent wording accepted, e.g. 'no condition to stop the function calling itself'.

levels.says: Vaguely mentions needing a stopping condition or that recursion never stops, without clearly saying the base case is absent or omitted.

points.description: States that an incorrectly defined recursive step causes infinite recursion, i.e. the recursive call does not move toward the base case (e.g. argument not reduced/changed, wrong update, or moves away so the base case is never reached). A vague 'wrong code' or 'error' alone does not earn this.

levels.says: Says the recursive step/call is wrong or faulty but does not explain that it fails to progress toward the base case.

rubric.notes: Two causes, each worth half: a missing base case, and a recursive step that does not progress toward the base case. Full marks for both stated clearly in any wording. Part marks for vague versions; no marks for unrelated causes like stack size or slow performance alone.

selftest_notes: The model answer scored only 3.5 of 5.
